brief: A shelf unit rated to hold 50 kg of books, with two drawers.

requirements.requirement: Shelf unit (storage made of hex bases with open bins/cells)
requirements.evidence: Four hex bases (piece: full at 0,0 / 1,0 / 0,1 and half-w at -1,0) with three open bins (bin:0,0,0 full, bin:0,1,0 full, bin:-1,0,0 half-w full) in the cells, all faces capped (10 solid caps) and joints bolted (3 jointBolts). check_build: ok, meshClash clear.

Two notch drawer frames (hex-drawer-frame-notch-mf) at the empty positions 1,-1 and 1,1, each between two touching bases. Drawer offers on half-base cut faces never appeared, so the notch drawer frames were used instead.

requirements.requirement: Rated to hold 50 kg of books
requirements.evidence: The configurator checks fit and collisions only and has no load rating or strength check. The printed plastic's capacity depends on the material and print settings the user chooses, so I cannot verify or claim a 50 kg rating. The build is a fit-checked layout only; a load test with the chosen material would be needed before loading it with books.
Book props would not rest in the bin cells (cell wall overlap) or on the bench at the positions tried, so no books were placed. The build has no props.

finish.summary: Built a fit-checked shelf unit: four hex bases, three open bins, two notch drawer frames, all faces capped and joints bolted; check_build is clean with meshClash clear. The 50 kg load rating cannot be verified by the configurator or established from the plastic shape, so that part is unmet. Books were not placed because the props would not rest in the cells.

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
